objectives: Find a name, number, time or place in a very short notice or message.
successCriteria: Reads all the words of the question before looking in the text
Finds the name, number, time or place that fits the whole question, not the first one of that type
Copies the answer from the text correctly
grammar: Wh-questions: who, what time, which day, where, how many
examples: The text says "Ali brings the ball at 5:15. The game starts at 5:30." The question "When does the game start?" needs 5:30, not 5:15.

items.prompt: Read the message. What day is the game?
items.material: Hi Mona! The football game is on Thursday. It is not on Monday this week. Ali brings the ball at 5:15. The game starts at 5:30. Meet me at the sports hall, not at the gate. Bring 3 friends and 1 bottle of water. From Jamal
acceptedAnswers: thursday

objectives: Find the main idea and specific details in a short email, timetable or story.
successCriteria: Chooses the main idea from the whole text, not from the first sentence
Finds the detail that fits all the words of the question
Gives a short answer of one or two words from the text
grammar: present and past simple in reading
going to / present continuous for plans
examples: The first sentence "Thank you for your nice letter." is a greeting. The main idea is the news in the middle of the email.

items.prompt: Read the email. What is it mostly about? (a) thanks for a letter (b) the family is moving (c) a room for guests
items.material: Dear Yasmin, Thank you for your nice letter. I have some news! Our family is moving to a new flat next month. The flat is on the fourth floor, and it has a big balcony. My new school is near the river, but my old school was next to the mosque. The moving day is on 14 May. My father starts his new job on 20 May. Can you visit us in June? We have a small room for guests now. Write soon! Love, Huda
acceptedAnswers: b

examples: My teacher is kind. She has short hair.
Our neighbour is old. He has a big garden.

objectives: Write a short text of 30-50 words about a routine, a past event or a plan, linking sentences with and, but and because.
successCriteria: Joins ideas with and, but or because chosen by meaning
Uses full stops: no long chain of "and"
Uses past verb forms for past events and present forms for routines
examples: Last summer we travelled to the mountains. It was cold at night, but the days were sunny.
I get up early because school starts at seven.
